description: Autonomous AI pentesting agents — real-time reconnaissance, vulnerability detection, and exploitation orchestration. Go + TypeScript.

written.description: Runs a second, independent agent whose only job is to re-exploit what the first one claimed, so a finding is either reproduced or dropped. One self-hosted binary with a local dashboard.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(agent): authoritative structured-surface enrichment for single-agent correctness (#756)

The single-agent architecture already derived obligations from the observed
surface, but the structured surface itself only fingerprinted endpoint lists:
methods were single-valued and sticky, parameters existed only for seeded
artifacts, and applicability-changing metadata observed AFTER the plan was
built could never reach the planner. With zero specialists the root agent
could therefore finish on a stale plan while a newly observed POST, XML
content type, or ?url= parameter should have opened new lanes.

Surface model (black-box first):

- Multi-method endpoint tracking: ObservedEndpointMethods is now a
  per-endpoint method SET (map[string]map[string]bool); a later observation
  never replaces or downgrades an earlier one (GET then POST keeps both).
- Runtime black-box parameter observation: query strings, form fields, JSON
  keys, multipart names, and python dict bodies enter ObservedEndpointParameters
  and drive applicability (url->SSRF/open-redirect, file->traversal,
  role->mass-assignment/privilege-escalation, id->IDOR). Parameter names are
  applicability SIGNALS, never vulnerability proof.
- Central observation path: every request-capable tool (terminal curl,
  python_action, http_request/send_request/browser/verify_*/authz_matrix)
  funnels method/content-type/parameter evidence through
  RecordSurfaceObservation, so no request path enriches the surface while
  another does not. Observed endpoints are promoted into the inventory with
  provenance (request/js/api/forms/context), and the notes-derived inventory
  is MERGED with the structured surface instead of replacing it - the
  structured surface is authoritative, notes remain the mirror.
- surfaceRevision now fingerprints every applicability-changing component:
  endpoints, per-endpoint methods, content types, observed parameters,
  seeded-surface methods+params, technologies, hosts, form evidence, and
  observed auth-flow families - all sorted, never map-iteration order.

Planner and ledger:

- Plan refresh now triggers on ANY semantic surface change, not only new
  endpoints (the revision covers methods/content types/params/auth flows).
- Mixed LLM+engine plans receive missing engine obligations incrementally
  via MergeRequiredEngineTasks: custom tasks, statuses, notes, and deps are
  preserved, engine tasks are only added when absent (idempotent, no
  duplicates), and recorded N/A skips are revalidated against the current
  surface and reopened when contradicted.
- Parameter-specific hypotheses are seeded for high-value parameters
  (SSRF on /fetch?url=, traversal on /download?file=, mass-assignment on
  role fields), deduped by (class, endpoint, parameter, role) and bounded.
- The finish gate refreshes the plan BEFORE evaluating completeness: a stale
  plan can never evaluate as complete once the surface moved under it.

Recon evidence and dispositions:

- Typed recon dispositions: the update_plan syntax now requires an explicit
  disposition keyword ("dimension: not_applicable - reason" or "dimension:
  blocked - reason"). Arbitrary prose after a colon ("api_surface: failed")
  is no longer laundered into N/A. Blocked and not_applicable are distinct
  typed terminal states; both settle a dimension, neither claims completion.
- N/A dispositions are validated against engine knowledge: API evidence
  blocks a false api_surface N/A, JS assets block js_analysis, an auth
  surface blocks auth_mapping, observed inputs block parameter_discovery,
  and a domain/wildcard scope blocks dismissing subdomain enumeration.
- crawlEvidence/techFingerprintEvidence/jsAnalysisEvidence: a 404 on
  robots.txt no longer completes crawling; dedicated crawlers complete on
  any non-error run (valid negative = zero routes); technology
  fingerprinting requires a deliberate action (whatweb/wappalyzer or a
  header fetch) - a random command containing "server:" is not coverage.
- JS analysis recognizes the download-to-file + rg/grep workflow, counts a
  real JS file with zero routes as a valid negative, and folds extracted
  routes/API paths into the structured surface with provenance.
- Auth mapping models observed FLOW FAMILIES (login, registration, logout,
  password-reset, oauth, mfa, token) instead of one boolean: a single /login
  response maps only the login family; credential availability stays a
  separate axis.
- Domain scope uses the Public Suffix List (golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix):
  example.co.uk is a registrable domain, *.example.co.uk scopes to
  example.co.uk and never to co.uk.
- Application-host prioritization is deterministic: candidates are gathered
  first, then ranked by role evidence and alphabetical tie-breaks, never by
  Go map iteration order.

Single-agent enforcement and skills:

- Zero specialists is now hard-enforced: spawn_agent/create_agent calls are
  rejected with a concise message when DelegationEnabled is false.
- The active lane gate makes methodology use deterministic: the next ready
  lane demands its methodology skill until read_skill SUCCEEDS - a delivered
  recommendation is not a loaded skill. Failed lookups stay retryable
  (bounded) instead of permanently suppressing the class methodology.

Tests: deterministic regression coverage for the whole contract (methods,
content types, parameters, mixed plans, typed dispositions, single-agent
enforcement, crawl/JS validation, auth flows, domain scope, host ranking,
lane skills, plan freshness). No offensive capability weakened; specialists
remain optional acceleration only; source assistance only enriches.
